transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. I guess what brings me in is that I’ve been feeling really restless, like all the time. Like I’m wound too tight and can’t quite settle down, even when I’m doing something that’s supposed to be calm.

It happens in planning meetings at work, which, I mean, those can be boring for anyone, but it’s more than that—I feel like I’m sort of buzzing under my skin. And even when I’m painting, which I usually enjoy, or trying to do yoga, I’m still… not settled. My body just doesn’t seem to get the message that I’m supposed to be calm.
Are you currently taking any prescription medications, especially any antipsychotic or anti-nausea drugs?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, I’m not on anything like that, as far as I know. Prescription-wise, no antipsychotic or anti-nausea medication that I can think of.

I did have a friend who was on something for nausea after surgery and she said it made her feel really strange, so I remember wondering about that kind of thing—but no, I’m not taking anything like that.

When you feel this restlessness, are you also experiencing a lot of worrying thoughts or fear about things going wrong, or is it more just a physical feeling of needing to move without particular worries attached?

It’s more physical, I think. Like, I’m not sitting there thinking, “Oh no, something terrible is going to happen,” exactly. It’s more like my body is just… wound too tight, like I can’t fully settle.

Like in planning meetings, I’ll be sitting there trying to look normal, and inside I’m buzzing. And it happens even with painting, which is supposed to be relaxing for me—or yoga, which is literally about calming down. I still feel like I need to move or shift or something. It’s not really attached to one specific worry.
Have you noticed any other physical changes lately, like feeling unusually hot, sweating more than normal, losing weight without trying, or your heart racing?

Um… I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed anything like that, at least not enough that I’d say, “Oh, that’s definitely happening.”

I mean, I do get warm sometimes, but I also work in retail buying and I’m running around or going between buildings, and sometimes the office temperature is ridiculous—like one room is freezing and the next is a sauna. So I’m not sure I’d know what counts as unusual.

But no, I haven’t noticed losing weight without trying or, like, dramatic sweating or anything. Heart racing… I don’t think so? Not in a way that stands out. Mostly it’s just the restless feeling.
Has this restless, buzzing feeling been something you've experienced since childhood or adolescence, or is this a new change that started more recently?

I think it goes way back, honestly. Like, I can remember in elementary school getting notes sent home because I kept popping out of my seat, or talking over other kids, or blurting out the answer before the teacher even finished asking the question.

And it’s funny, I still remember one teacher had this whole color-card behavior chart thing—sorry, that’s probably not the point—but yeah, it wasn’t just something that started recently. It was there when I was little too.
Do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks, lose track of what you're doing, or forget things like appointments or where you put items?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I lose my phone around the house sometimes, but I feel like everyone does that—especially when you set it down “just for a second” and then it’s somehow under a catalog or in the kitchen.

Appointments… I don’t know that I’ve noticed a big pattern there. My work calendar is kind of packed and color-coded, and honestly half of retail buying is just juggling dates and emails and samples and—sorry, I’m drifting.

I guess I’d say I haven’t really noticed it as a major thing, but maybe I’d need to think about what you mean by “often.”
Would you say these restlessness and focus issues have caused real problems for you both at work and in your personal life outside of work, like with relationships or daily responsibilities at home?

Yeah… I think so, though I wouldn’t say it’s like everything is falling apart.

At work, it’s shown up with purchase orders where I’ve had to get corrections made, and my planning coordinator has had to kind of double-check things more than I’d like. Which is embarrassing, because I do know how to do my job, it’s just sometimes I’m moving too fast or jumping ahead.

And at home… family dinners can get tense. I don’t mean to, but people feel like I’m talking over them, or cutting in before they’re done. Then I feel bad, and then I try to explain, and that can turn into another whole thing. So yes, I guess it has caused problems in both places.

Do you often find yourself making careless mistakes on detailed tasks, or getting easily distracted and losing focus even when you're trying hard to pay attention, like during meetings or while reading something important?

Yeah, that part does happen. Especially with detailed work stuff.

Like over the past couple of years, I’ll swear I checked a vendor spreadsheet carefully, and then my planning coordinator catches something after the fact—like I transposed a SKU, or I missed a freight surcharge, or I carried the wrong quantity into the purchase order.

And the annoying thing is, I’m not being careless on purpose. I’ll be sitting there thinking, okay, I’ve reviewed this, it’s fine—and then there’s some tiny thing that isn’t tiny once it affects an order. It’s embarrassing, honestly.

The combination of hyperactive-impulsive and inattentive symptoms with childhood onset and current impairment supports combined presentation ADHD.
